reviewer.tool: agent image read tool on the captured PNGs listed below; numeric Debug sun/channel readback, the T30 directional report and the generated/external capture manifest

observations: The controlled directional-probe wall is a set of flat, constant-normal panels. Its Lambert direct response stays at the same numeric value (1.038) across camera orbit yaws 0/20/40/60 while the sun stays at azimuth 0.75, elevation 0.45. The sun does not follow the camera.

At a stationary camera, moving the sun from front (0.75) through side (0.875/1.0) to behind (0.25) reduces the Lambert direct term monotonically to zero. Clearcoat direct changes in the same direction (front 0.0166 linear vs 0.0012 ambient-only behind), so the base and coat lobes share one sun instead of the old Studio key.

The horizontal floor panel brightens as elevation rises from 0.15 to 1.2 rad. The orbit sequence keeps the camera orientation's up axis and the wall/floor relation stable; no clipped, NaN or black discontinuity appears in any sweep.

The zero-intensity capture is black for every lit panel and the floor, while the emissive panel keeps its authored magenta emission. No flat ambient wash survives, and no channel reads a negative or non-finite value.

Gold metal keeps a Fresnel/BRDF-weighted ambient reflection well above black paint (env specular 0.021 vs 0.0012 luma at the same view). Black paint remains dark (max linear <0.12), and thin glass keeps its own transmitted/reflection channel. Metals remain visible without washing black paint or glass to white.

Studio and Directional at the same camera/fixture have a measured mean-luma ratio of about 1.10; exposure and tone-map state are unchanged by the mode switch. The two modes share the same IBL floor, so the difference is the single direct sun.

The mode switch and an imported-up-axis change preserve the global sun azimuth/elevation. Opening another asset keeps the Directional mode and sun state; there is no per-asset light exception. The up-axis command deliberately refits bounds and resets the camera to the new home view, which is recorded separately from the sun state.

Car: red paint and dark trim separate under both front and back sun; windshield/roof/side-glass detail remains visible without a flat white wash. The known authored window/roof speckles also appear in Studio and are unchanged by this work.
Camera: the black body, lens ring and lens recess keep dark-side depth and a visible reflection; the leather strap remains legible against the dark backdrop. The lens is not turned into a white disk.
Microscope: brass and black enamel retain part separation and cavity detail at elevation 0.62 in both front and back sun. This run loaded the asset completely; no ResourceLimit overlay occurred.

CAD relief: the STL plate front/back views show clearly different face shading and readable chamfers/raised inner plate; the STEP assembly shows lit and shadowed red faces. The generated stl-box directional oblique view keeps hard edges and planar face contrast.

The analytic ground contact shadow now follows the same world sun: the Directional ground ellipse shifts when azimuth changes and is absent when the shadow layer is turned off. It remains a bounds-projected presentation cue rather than a geometry-accurate shadow (T31).
No asset-name or material-name exception is present in the renderer or the lane.

defects.label: known-defect
defects.where: Car windshield/roof/window edges in Studio and Directional
defects.description: Small bright speckles along authored window/trim seams remain. They also appear in Studio and are not caused by the Directional sun transform; they are an authored-geometry/edge-quality defect.

defects.label: limitation
defects.description: The shadow is still the T16 analytic bounds ellipse projected along the correct world sun, not a geometry-derived occluder. T31 owns the geometry-derived contact shadow and must keep consuming the same sun direction.

defects.label: known-defect
defects.description: The external microscope can still report a terminal generation deadline after visible geometry on slower runs. This T30 run loaded it completely and produced the brass/enamel crops; a future late failure stays a non-passing observation.

positives: One documented world-space Z-up sun direction drives the base and clearcoat direct lobes, the nav-gizmo bearing, the legacy compact shader and the contact-shadow input.
The shading vectors are world-frame with a camera-relative origin, so the camera transform lives in the view matrix; the sun is used directly and a stationary sun cannot orbit with the camera.
Light/environment intensity zero removes direct, IBL, clearcoat and the background-only transmission fallback while preserving emission.
The environment response remains the T24 split-sum Fresnel/BRDF path; no second unweighted reflection or leftover Studio key was added to Directional.

Sun controls, keyboard/accessibility paths and the existing gizmo ring/sun drag behaviour are unchanged; the new Debug fields 277/278 are read/write state only and remain inside the Debug test-control guard.
